- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast spikes; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike, model often over-anticipates continuation; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underreacts; increase forecast by 2–5% to capture momentum.
- Model consistently under-forecasts mean-reversion zones; if recent 3–5 days show strong mean reversion, add 1–2% upward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–2 days; shift forecast up by 0.5–1.5% for next period if sentiment is neutral or bullish.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model over-smooths; use 1–2% higher forecast to capture volatility.
- When sentiment drops sharply after a peak, model fails to correct; add 1–3% downward bias to prevent over-optimism.
